item.title: Paul Skenes caps awful month with another brutal start, and an alarming stat has MLB fans concerned
item.description: Paul Skenes hasn't topped 98 MPH in his last four starts after doing so nearly 900 times last year, and his ERA has ballooned to 3.90 this season.
item.content:encoded:
It's officially August, and MLB fans are officially worried about Paul Skenes.

Not great!

The ace of the Pittsburgh Pirates got rocked again Friday night, giving up five runs on seven hits in a loss to the Cincinnati Reds. It marked the second straight start in which Skenes gave up five runs, and capped a brutal month for the 24-year-old in which he gave up at least five runs in three of his five starts.

Skenes' ERA is now 3.90 — a full two runs higher than both his 2024 and 2025 totals.

To be fair, the ace did have three good starts last month, going 3-0 in the middle of the month with just a total of five earned runs in those three games. So, it's not all bad. It's not all doom and gloom.

Things could certainly be worse.

But ... something is off, and one troubling stat hit the internet last night that has baseball fans worried on this first day of August:

Lordy. I had to refresh the page just to make sure those stats were correct.

Paul Skenes hasn't topped 98 MPH in his last four starts, and he's topped it only 95 times this season. He did it nearly 900 times last year, and nearly 700 the year before.

It's a jarring number to see, regardless of what you think of Skenes' season. He routinely had one of the liveliest fastballs in the league for two years, and the velocity just isn't there this season.

Of course, some of it could be by design. Skenes admitted as much last month, when questions first started to pop up about his fastball.

"It's been by design," he told DK Pittsburgh Sports. "It's nothing I've been worried about."

Still, the numbers are the numbers — as they say — and they're alarming to see. He capped his worst month as a professional last night by giving up five runs in back-to-back games for the first time in his career, and lasted just four innings.

Here's another stat that the fellas in Pittsburgh's analytics department won't love: Skenes gave up just 41 earned runs all of last year. Through 23 starts in 2026, he's already given up 54.

A blip? A bad season? Or real cause for concern?

Pirates pre- and post-game host, Dan Zangrilli, didn't mince words after the loss:

"The ace didn't ace," he said. "Far more questions than answers. For any of this to work, he has to. He looks like an out of shape, lumbering yeti sucking wind on a hot day."

Goodness gracious. What a takedown. Just a scathing review from someone who is around the team all the time.

Is it fair? I don't know. But things aren't going great right now in Pittsburgh on this first day of August.

item.title: Nicki Minaj torches Anthony Fauci in mock diary video after explosive Senate appearance
item.description: Nicki Minaj shared a satirical video mocking Anthony Fauci's diary entries days after he invoked the Fifth Amendment over 100 times at a Senate hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj is once again taking aim at Dr. Anthony Fauci. 

She escalated her criticism of the former White House COVID-19 advisor with a satirical video and a series of social media posts following his recent Senate testimony.

On Friday, the rapper shared a video filmed in near darkness in which she pretended to be Fauci writing in a diary.

INSIDE FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY: WHAT HE WROTE ABOUT TRUMP, TV PERSONALITIES AND CELEBRITIES

"Dear Diary, well the press is hot for me," Minaj started the clip while impersonating the longtime public health official.

Continuing the parody, she added, "They say I'm sexier than Tyra Banks. Julia Roberts gasped when she saw how handsome I was. Brad Pitt played me on 'SNL.'"

The jokes quickly turned into criticism of Fauci's pandemic leadership.

"Never mind that I sent millions of children back years on their education ... the elderly are alone and afraid, dying by themselves," Minaj said before delivering one final jab: "If anyone asks questions, me and my gang ruins their lives."

The video came days after Fauci appeared before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, where he invoked the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times during questioning about his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The hearing followed the release of Fauci's pandemic-era diary by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky. The entries detail his meetings and observations throughout the pandemic, including reflections on his public profile and discussions about COVID-19's origins.

NICKI MINAJ ACCUSES CALIFORNIA GOV. NEWSOM OF 'TRYING TO BE TRUMP' IN SCATHING INTERVIEW

Republicans have since intensified their criticism of Fauci, with Rep. Rich McCormick, R-Ga., introducing legislation that would bar him from returning to government service and potentially expose him to criminal prosecution.

Minaj continued to pile on with a series of posts on X.

In one, she mocked the government's COVID-19 booster recommendations, writing, "They started telling yall to get a new booster shot every 5 to 10 business days like it was the new Jordans droppin?!?!!!!!!! That's when I knew. I went in my backyard & started building the Arc. Nicki's Arc. I know the Lord won't send another flood but still."

In another post, she blamed Fauci for lasting emotional and societal damage she believes he caused during the pandemic.

"Feeding tubes will be his portion. He will lose the ability to speak & then & only then will he feel the collective pain & long term ramifications he caused to new borns, young children who are still trying to become acclimated into society & schools, traumatized pregnant women who couldn’t even have family in the delivery rooms & visits, the elderly who died alone & afraid," she wrote.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

She continued, "...young ppl still struggling w/mental health, suicide, people turned away from hospitals at their most vulnerable moments, the trust that is now gone from innocent people toward their governments forever, billions of stolen money from hard working tax payers via con artists…I’ve been struggling to find the humor in any of this. God bless everyone who made it to the other side. You’re stronger than you thought. God is in control."

The post also featured an AI-generated image of Fauci in a '90s-inspired bedroom, writing in a diary — a clear nod to the recently released journals that have been the focus of political debate.

The posts quickly drew both praise and backlash.

One supporter wrote, "Nicki getting that shot is one of the biggest regrets of my life. I was under so much stress during that time & was threatened with unemployment that I buckled & took it. Only God knows the impact it's had on my body. We deserve justice."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Minaj replied, "I don’t want you guys to beat up on yourselves. You did what you had to do to feed your family. You had no choice. Now take it to God in prayer & trust that by his stripes you are healed. In Jesus name, Amen. love you guys. And yes! Justice is imperative!!!!!!!!!" 

Actor Rob Schneider also weighed in on her statements, writing on X, "Nicki is a rarity in show business, a real truth teller!!"

However, not everyone agreed with the rapper's remarks.

"We studied science. You sang songs. We aren’t the same. Stay in [your] lane," one critic wrote.

Another user added, "You attacking Dr. Fauci is beyond laughable. You’ve… embarrassed yourself spreading baseless vaccine claims, and somehow convinced yourself that celebrity makes you an authority on public health. Fauci has 50+ years of science and public service behind him. You have scandals and a social media account."

Minaj has repeatedly challenged Fauci and COVID-19 policies since the pandemic, and her latest barrage makes clear the feud between the two is far from over.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham supporters rallied outside in Portland while liberal fans booed her inside
item.description: Dozens rallied outside Portland's Moda Center in support of Sophie Cunningham's stance on women's sports as trans supporters clashed nearby.
item.content:encoded:
Sophie Cunningham is now the most polarizing athlete in sports. She’s loved and she’s hated. That was clear Friday evening in Portland as the Fever traveled to another liberal Mecca to play one of the WNBA’s newest expansion franchises, the Portland Fire.

Cunningham’s bold stance to support the effort to keep women’s sports and spaces female has attracted women’s sports advocates to rally outside of her games. The first rally, which took place in Seattle, received moderate pushback from trans supporters and made headlines due to what happened inside the arena. A now fined and suspended co-owner of the Seattle Storm, Celeste Keaton, berated two teenage girls sitting courtside with XX-XY Athletics T-shirts and a sign that said, "Thank You Sophie For Speaking Up For Girls." Meanwhile, a local store director of Nordstrom, Marco Esquivel, was caught berating and cussing at the girls, their mothers and fellow Cunningham supporters. Nordstrom has yet to make a public statement.

"The 'With Love Is Truth' series began July 28, 2026, when women’s rights group Women Are Real, women’s rights advocate Amy E. Sousa (AKA Known Heretic), and independent journalist Brandi Kruse organized a fan rally with local supporters, including Washington high school athletes, outside Climate Pledge Arena before the Indiana Fever’s game against the Seattle Storm," the group stated via a press release.

"We are here today [in Portland] in solidarity with those girls [who were berated in Seattle], in solidarity with Sophie Cunningham, and in solidarity with all female athletes," Sousa stated proudly as she addressed the crowd outside the arena.

Sousa was joined Friday by dozens of individuals directly associated with the group, including former Olympian Inga Thompson and attorney Kara Dansky - a board member of Democrats for an Informed Approach to Gender and former president of Women’s Declaration International USA, outside the Moda Center. They had dozens more join in support of the group’s efforts and Cunningham’s stance about 90 minutes before tip-off.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY ROCKS WNBA GAME AS 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS FACE COUNTERPROTEST

Sousa said that Cunningham has been, "a voice of reason, in what has become a very contentious topic." She was then rudely interrupted by a woman in a "Protect Trans Kids" shirt, which featured a rose and a knife. The shirt has been worn by Minnesota Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan and the apparel features a rose and a knife to show that advocates will use both support and active, militant resistance to keep trans children safe from harm. The protester was one of about a dozen trans supporters who joined in opposition to the Cunningham supporters.

The trans supporters I talked to were not interested in defending their stance that men should be allowed in women’s sports. Many of them cussed at me, as if having dialogue is not allowed. One protestor in a frog suit, holding a sign that said, "Trans People Just Want To Live" responded to my questioning by saying I’m promoting a "bulls*** issue."

Other trans-supporting protesters I spoke with tried deflecting my questioning about why they supported men in women’s sports, and one even said it was possible for a biological man to change his chromosomes to become a woman.

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

One photographer, who works for the Associated Press, told me that a group of young boys and girls didn’t know what they were doing holding signs, which stated "Thank You Sophie" with hearts on it, insinuating that they were essentially indoctrinated into this position to support Cunningham and keeping sports female, by their parents and the organizing group.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS BLUNT MESSAGE TO BOOING, TRANS FLAG-WAVING WNBA CROWD AFTER DRILLING SHOT

So, I went up to the group, which included 6 young girls, 3 mothers, and one young boy, to ask them. Answering my question about why they were there and if they understood what they were supporting, one of the girls stated boldly, "No boys and girls in the same sports. Like no boys in girls sports." The Associated Press photographer stood by, off camera, defeated, though he tried to backtrack.

Cunningham stated pregame, "I'm here to play basketball, but I'm also here to be me, and I'm not going to like shadow that or hide or, you know, dim my light just because maybe people don't agree with that."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Inside the arena for the game, Cunningham received relentless boos every time she checked in and touched the ball. The Fire promoted trans and gay pride flags held by fans whenever they could, clearly showcasing their anti-Cunningham agenda. The loudest cheer of the evening, up to that point, was during the ultra-inclusive "companion cam," featuring multiple gay couples kissing and a group of lesbian trans supporters waving trans flags prior to the start of the second quarter.

It was evident that many fans were there to protest Cunningham's "common sense" stance. The protests didn't stop outside. That was clear in the apparel, flags, and voices of the Fire fans in the building.

The next rally is slated for Sunday in Minnesota as the Fever play the red-hot Minnesota Lynx.

item.title: Humanoid robot skin senses people before contact
item.description: Gene.01's sensor-filled smart skin detects workers before contact occurs, but Generative Bionics has yet to release detailed workplace safety data.
item.content:encoded:
Working beside a metal humanoid robot would probably make you watch every step it takes. After all, a collision between a heavy robot and a human body will usually end worse for the person. Italian startup Generative Bionics believes its Gene.01 humanoid robot could help reduce that risk. The company covered the robot with sensor-filled skin that can detect a person approaching before physical contact occurs.

The system also senses touch, temperature and force. As a result, Gene.01 can gather information about what surrounds its body and what happens during an interaction. That sounds reassuring. However, the real question is whether the sensors and control software can react quickly enough when people start working beside the robot.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class "Sick of Spam?" has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You'll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

WEARABLE PATCH VIBRATES WHEN DANGER IS NEARBY

Gene.01 carries distributed sensors across its torso and limbs. The company says this smart skin detects touch, temperature, proximity and force at the same time. Proximity sensing gives the robot an early warning when someone enters the space around its body.

The basic idea feels familiar. You may feel heat near a stove and pull your hand away before touching the surface. In a similar way, Gene.01 can detect a nearby person before the person touches its sensor-covered body. That information gives the robot's control system a chance to respond before contact. It can also continue measuring force if contact happens. However, Generative Bionics has not released detailed workplace safety data showing how the system performs during full industrial shifts. For now, the safety benefits remain company claims tied to a newly introduced platform.

Traditional factory robots often operate behind barriers to keep workers outside their range of motion. Humanoid robots create a different challenge. Companies want these machines to use tools and move through spaces built for people. That could place them closer to human workers.

Cameras can help a robot see someone approaching. However, a camera may lose sight of a person who stands too close or moves behind part of the robot. Full-body proximity sensing adds another source of information. The robot can detect activity near its torso or limbs without depending entirely on its view of the room.

HUMANOID ROBOT VIDEOS SHOW MACHINES LASHING OUT

Gene.01's sensors could also change how workers teach a humanoid robot. A person can guide the robot's arm through a movement while the system records the motion and force involved. This gives the robot information that a video demonstration may leave out.

For example, a video can show a robot where to place its hand. Yet the footage may not reveal how tightly the robot should grip an object. Too little pressure could cause the item to slip. Excessive force could damage it.

By moving Gene.01's arm directly, a worker can demonstrate the physical feel of the task. The company says this approach can help the robot learn how much force to apply. That could make robot training more accessible to experienced workers who understand the job but do not program robots.

Generative Bionics built Gene.01 around an approach it calls Physical AI. Under this approach, engineers develop the robot's body and movement controls as a connected system. They do not build the hardware first and treat the software as a separate layer added later.

The team uses models of the robot and its human partner. It can then adjust the design around measurable factors such as walking stability and physical strain on the person. The approach grew from research conducted by members of the company's founding team at the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia.

Nature Machine Intelligence published that research on July 13, 2026. The paper focuses on a human-aware robot called ergoCub rather than Gene.01. Researchers jointly optimized ergoCub's physical design and movement controls. They used human-related measurements, including stress on a person's back, alongside the robot's walking requirements. Generative Bionics says Gene.01 is the first industrial platform to apply that peer-reviewed methodology to a fully functional humanoid covered in sensors.

The company says its team moved Gene.01 from a concept to a functional platform in six months. Generative Bionics CEO Daniele Pucci said the company designed the robot as a foundation for different industrial machines.

"Unlike other one-size fits all humanoids, Gene.01 is a scalable platform, customized at the edge of AI, design and end-effector level to maximize each customer's needs. It is also the first expression of our belief that Physical AI must be human-aware, physics-native and industrial from day one. In six months, our team moved from concept to a fully functional and sensorized humanoid platform by combining deep humanoid robotics expertise with AI, biomechanics and design." Pucci said the company wants robots to learn from the physical world while adapting to each customer's work.

Generative Bionics designed Gene.01 as a base for a family of specialized humanoids. The company can adjust the AI for a particular task. It can also alter the robot's exterior to fit the working environment.

Meanwhile, engineers can replace its end effectors. That technical term covers the hands, grippers or feet attached to the ends of a robot's limbs. A robot built for warehouse work may need a different hand than one designed to operate welding equipment. This platform approach lets Generative Bionics adapt one core robot instead of designing every machine from the ground up.

The company sees potential uses in manufacturing and logistics. It has also identified inspection, public safety and health care as possible future markets. However, Gene.01 remains an early industrial platform. Generative Bionics still needs to show that its customization strategy can work reliably outside controlled demonstrations.

Generative Bionics has also started releasing a digital model of Gene.01. The model lets developers simulate the robot before they gain access to the physical machine. They can test movement software and begin developing industry-specific applications in a virtual environment.

The company's website currently links to a preview of the robot's URDF model on GitHub. URDF stands for Unified Robot Description Format. Developers use it to describe a robot's physical structure for software and simulation tools. Generative Bionics says it wants to maintain the model across software distribution systems that Physical AI developers already use. An open model could attract researchers and robotics developers to the platform.

Gene.01's first planned industrial use involves shipbuilding. Generative Bionics is working with Italian shipbuilding company Fincantieri to develop a humanoid for welding operations in shipyards. Shipyards can contain tight work areas and heavy equipment. Welding also exposes workers to heat and fumes. A humanoid could eventually handle selected tasks in areas that place extra physical demands on people. However, Generative Bionics and Fincantieri have not yet published detailed performance results from the welding project. The partnership will give Gene.01 an important test.

Generative Bionics has raised an $81 million seed round led by CDP Venture Capital. AMD Ventures, Duferco and Eni Next participated in the round. RoboIT and Tether also invested. That funding gives the company more resources to develop Gene.01 and expand its production capacity. Generative Bionics says its team includes about 100 people. Nearly half hold doctoral degrees, according to the company. The team's experience includes earlier humanoid projects such as iCub and ergoCub.

The company also wants to build more of its humanoid technology in Europe. Generative Bionics formed a strategic partnership with German company Synapticon to develop an actuation system for Gene.01 and future robots. Actuators serve as the motorized joints that move a robot's body. They play an important role in how quickly and forcefully a humanoid can move. The partnership covers final assembly and calibration in Europe. The companies also plan to conduct safety testing there. Generative Bionics says this approach will give it more control over key components while supporting European compliance requirements.

You probably will not find Gene.01 working beside you tomorrow. Still, its sensing skin points to a larger change in humanoid robot design. Companies want these machines to move beyond fenced-off areas and enter workplaces built for people. To do that safely, robots need more awareness of the humans standing around them. Detecting a worker before contact gives the machine more time to react. Force sensing could also help the robot respond more carefully when physical interaction occurs.

Gene.01 introduces a promising idea for factory safety. Its sensor-filled skin can detect a nearby person before physical contact and continue measuring force during an interaction. The system could also help workers teach the robot by physically guiding its movements. That gives Gene.01 information about force that video demonstrations may miss. However, most of the performance and safety details currently come from Generative Bionics. The company now needs to support those claims with workplace testing and clear data. Smart skin may give a humanoid more awareness of the person beside it. Yet awareness only helps when the robot reacts correctly every time.

Would you trust smart skin to protect you from a full-size humanoid at work, or would you still want a barrier between you and the machine? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: Why Fauci's 111 Fifth Amendment pleas could end up before the courts
item.description: Anthony Fauci's Fifth Amendment invocations drew parallels to Lois Lerner's case, raising questions about whether Trump's DOJ will prosecute.
item.content:encoded:
Silence is golden.

But actions speak louder than words.

That’s the solution which Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., is engineering for the reticence of Dr. Anthony Fauci. The head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for 38 years, Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment a staggering 111 times when appearing under subpoena before Paul’s panel this week.

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

The only words Fauci spoke were his invocation of the Fifth Amendment on the advice of his attorney. But the action promised by Paul is contempt of Congress.

"There will be repercussions to your refusal to testify today," warned Paul after Fauci invoked the Fifth. "The Committee will have to consider after this hearing what appropriate action should be taken against you for the failure to testify after being directed to do so. It's against the law to obstruct an investigation of Congress."

But it’s not as though Fauci was completely mum during the entire hearing. He offered an opening statement before leaning on the Fifth Amendment as a shield for the next three hours.

"The only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, ‘behind bars,’ unquote," Fauci said. "Any reasonable person who has followed his unhinged obsession with me would readily come to the same conclusion."

And then Fauci fell mute. He ignored questions about his diary, inquiries about what ignited the pandemic, even interrogatives about the mundane.

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

"What day of the week is it today?" asked Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo.

Hawley wasn’t done.

"What color tie are you're wearing?" Hawley continued. "What is the color of the carpeting?"

From a legal standpoint, there is logic behind Hawley’s banal inquiries. These are carefully designed questions which a good prosecutor might ask a witness to trip them up.

To wit: If Fauci had already invoked the Fifth Amendment, why is he suddenly answering questions about the calendar, his tie or carpeting? If Fauci replied "Wednesday," "blue" or "green" as answers to Hawley’s queries, Paul could have asserted that the Fifth Amendment shield no longer applied. Thus, the committee, or the courts, should compel Fauci to respond to any question.

By the same token, Republicans argued that Fauci should have been able to answer such trite questions from Hawley because they had nothing to do with the proceedings. It’s kind of a "we win, you lose" proposition for the GOP.

Yet Fauci never deviated from the script, invoking the Fifth Amendment 111 times.

CAN FAUCI HIDE BEHIND THE FIFTH? GAME-CHANGING BIDEN PARDON MAY NOT PROVIDE COMPLETE COVER, EXPERTS SAY

By the way, Fauci’s repetitive legal recitation of the Fifth is not a Senate record. In 1958, mob boss Vito Genovese appeared before a Senate panel investigating organized crime. Genovese established the mark, invoking the Fifth a stupefying 150 times.

Republicans don’t think that Fauci had any right to invoke the Fifth even once, considering his pardon from former President Joe Biden. On one hand, they asserted he should be free to testify. Democrats took issue with that.

"I’m not surprised that he pled the Fifth because the objective is to put him in jeopardy of criminal prosecution," said Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn. "So the more prudent course was to claim the Fifth Amendment."

Hawley saw it differently, citing the 1896 Supreme Court case Brown v. Walker.

In the late 19th Century, the Supreme Court granted auditor Theodore Brown immunity to testify in a railway rate-fixing case. But Brown still refused to testify. However, the High Court ruled that Brown had to speak. Writing for the majority, Justice Henry Billings Brown (no relation), who also wrote the opinion in Plessy v. Ferguson, declared the following:

"If it be once conceded that the fact that his testimony may tend to bring the witness into disrepute, though not to incriminate him, does not entitle him to the privilege of silence, it necessarily follows that, if it also tends to incriminate, but at the same time operates as a pardon for the offense, the fact that the disgrace remains no more entitles him to immunity in this case than in the other."

Translation: What you have to say may be embarrassing. But if you enjoy the privilege of immunity, you still have to cough up the goods, despite the Fifth Amendment.

How Fauci conducted himself in the hearing runs parallel to former IRS official Lois Lerner's conduct in 2014. Republicans believed that Lerner blocked groups affiliated with the Tea Party from tax-exempt status or targeted them for scrutiny. At a 2014 House Oversight Committee hearing, Lerner delivered an opening statement. She then invoked the Fifth.

The full House later voted to hold Lerner in contempt of Congress for not answering questions and referred her to the Justice Department for prosecution. The DOJ, then operating under the administration of former President Barack Obama, did not take action against Lerner.

Whether or not DOJ prosecutes contempt of Congress often comes down to which party on Capitol Hill is doing the referring, and which party controls the Justice Department.

For instance, the Republican House referred former Attorney General Eric Holder to the DOJ for contempt of Congress in 2012. But it was Holder who ran the Justice Department. So that was a dead letter.

The Democratic House referred White House Counsel Harriet Miers to the DOJ in 2008. But the administration of former President George W. Bush was simply not going to prosecute its own lead attorney at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave.

The Democratic House held Trump administration figures Steve Bannon and Peter Navarro in contempt of Congress for failing to appear before the committee investigating the Jan. 6 riot. Naturally, the Biden Justice Department prosecuted that duo.

So could Fauci face prosecution from the Trump Justice Department after a referral from the Republican-led Senate?

The Lerner case bears further study. The Obama DOJ declined to prosecute Lerner because she asserted her Fifth Amendment rights — but after her opening statement. Fauci did the same. Would the Trump administration perceive Fauci’s protocol at the hearing through a similar lens?

Paul will ask his committee to prep a resolution holding Fauci in contempt of Congress in the coming days. But the full Senate must approve such a measure before sending it to the DOJ for possible prosecution.

It’s easier to adopt a contempt of Congress resolution in the House because it only requires a simple majority. The same is true in the Senate. But it must also clear a filibuster, which needs 60 votes. That’s why contempt of Congress citations are more prevalent in the House than the Senate.

But Paul believes he has a workaround.

"I plan on sending it directly with the legal brief supporting the argument to the Department of Justice," Paul told Fox News.

It’s then up to DOJ to prosecute Fauci or not.

However, in his same appearance on Fox, Paul said he had "sent a criminal referral on Anthony Fauci twice under Biden and twice under Trump."

President Donald Trump’s DOJ hasn’t prosecuted Fauci before. But would prosecutors see it differently after Fauci’s performance at the hearing?

That brings us back to Lerner.

She invoked the Fifth Amendment and the DOJ did not prosecute. That establishes a precedent. Would the Trump DOJ follow that model? Or are we in for what could be a lengthy, perhaps seminal court battle about whether Fauci was in the right to invoke the Fifth Amendment? That may trigger a legal fight over his pardon from Biden — and perhaps what the High Court ruled in Brown v. Walker.

We’ll know when or if the DOJ takes action. In the case of Fauci, silence may be golden. But in this instance, it may be up to the courts to determine if it’s legal.

item.title: Three big college football recruiting 'winners' that helped their cases in the month of July
item.description: Miami Hurricanes landed their fifth five-star recruit in the 2027 class, while Indiana and Florida State made historic recruiting gains in July.
item.content:encoded:
A quick glance at your calendar (if you still have one of those hanging around) will inform you that we have now entered the month of August, which means college football is exactly four weeks away.

It's an exciting time to be a fan, as fall camp starts to ramp up and practice reports will have every fanbase believing this is the year their team wins it all, but there's plenty of action off the field to be locked in on too, namely recruiting.

Nowadays, most of the top-end talent in the current recruiting class has already committed to their program of choice by mid summer, but that doesn't mean we still didn't see some July fireworks on the recruiting trail.

FIVE-STAR TEXAS A&M OFFENSIVE LINE COMMIT GETS TORCHED ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR AWKWARD HAT RITUAL

Here are three college football programs that picked up big wins in the class of 2027 this past month.

After a blistering June on the recruiting trail, Mario Cristobal and company seemed like they might have taken the month of July off for a little vacation.

Who could blame them? After all, they were sitting comfortably within the top five of most recruiting industry rankings and their class was nearly full with 20 commits.

DON'T BURY TEXAS TECH JUST YET: RED RAIDERS SHOULD STILL BE CFP CONTENDERS, EVEN WITHOUT BRENDAN SORSBY

Then, about a week or so ago, some of the more plugged-in sources in the recruiting world started making noise about five-star cornerback A'mir Sears reclassifying from 2028 to 2027.

Given his South Florida roots and the fact that the Canes were seen as the leader to land his commitment even a year out, alarm bells started ringing that Miami's elite 2027 class was about to reach another level.

Then, on the last day of July, Sears decided to make it official, giving the Hurricanes their fifth five-star and putting the rest of the country on notice that The U might really be back this time.

FIVE IMPACT FRESHMEN FROM THE SEC WHO ARE SURE TO TURN HEADS ON THE FIELD THIS COMING SEASON

I didn't think it was possible for anyone to catch the Texas A&M Aggies, but Miami has a serious shot.

item.title: Trump blasts rogue GOP senators for blocking Blanche nomination, vows anti-weaponization bill fight
item.description: Trump vows to keep Todd Blanche as acting attorney general and revive the $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund if John Cornyn and Thom Tillis block him.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump blasted Sens. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, on Saturday for opposing his nomination of Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to the permanent position, suggesting he could keep Blanche in the temporary Justice Department leadership role and ensure the Anti-Weaponization Bill is passed.

While blasting the rogue GOP senators, Trump tied the Blanche nomination fight to the Anti-Weaponization Bill, proposed legislation that would establish a congressionally authorized compensation program for alleged victims of political "weaponization," replacing the controversial DOJ-created Anti-Weaponization Fund.

The fund was formed through a settlement Blanche reached with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Treasury Department to create a $1.8 billion fund to compensate alleged victims of political persecution. Amid criticism that the executive branch lacked authority to create such a program without congressional approval, the Justice Department later said it would not move forward with the fund, effectively shelving it.

"If Senators Cornyn and Tillis, both upset because I wouldn’t Endorse them (they lost, and quit, respectively!), aren’t going to approve Todd Blanche, one of the most respected professionals, according to everybody, in the Country, to be the United States Attorney General, then I will keep Todd as Acting A.G., and push hard to get the Anti-Weaponization Bill, which takes care of those who have been so badly treated by the Crooked Joe Biden (and Obuma!) Administration (I get nothing, although I was treated horribly!), PASSED. Todd Blanche was a voice of reason! It will immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done," Trump wrote in a Saturday morning post on Truth Social.

TRUMP THREATENS TO YANK HIS OWN AG NOMINEE AS GOP REVOLT GROWS

Cornyn and Tillis, both of whom faced electoral opposition from Trump in some form, each indicated that they would not vote to advance Blanche's nomination out of the Senate Judiciary Committee.

"I think I am prepared to vote no, but I do think I owe it to my constituents and to Mr. Blanche to try to negotiate in good faith," Cornyn told Capitol Hill reporters on Wednesday. "And that’s what we’ve been doing. And so we’ll see where things are this morning and see where we go from here," he added.

Though both Blanche and Trump have previously said the Anti-Weaponization Fund is "dead," Cornyn and Tillis both indicated that they want the fund's demise to be formalized in writing before supporting Blanche's confirmation.

Cornyn questioned Blanche about the fund during his mid-July confirmation hearing.

"Has there been a written agreement of the parties to modify the settlement fund?" Cornyn asked Blanche.

"No, the settlement fund is just not moving forward," Blanche replied.

TRUMP UNLOADS ON CORNYN, TIES AG NOMINATION FIGHT TO BITTER TEXAS PRIMARY

Tillis, who announced in 2025 that he would not be seeking re-election just one day after Trump threatened to back a primary challenger, also criticized the Anti-Weaponization Fund, calling it a "payout pot for punks" in a Saturday morning response to Trump on X.

"Despite comments as late as yesterday that the fund is dead, President Trump clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against. It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal. Hopefully, we can resolve this by Tuesday," Tillis wrote

Cornyn, who has been a senator since 2002, lost his GOP primary to Trump-backed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton during the state's May 26 contest, losing by nearly 400,000 votes, according to the Texas Secretary of State's Office.

Trump, during his Friday Cabinet meeting at Camp David, theorized that his backing of Paxton was Cornyn's motivation for opposing Blanche.

"This is being done by a senator. And I don't really blame him, to be honest with you. I endorsed his opponent. And as soon as I endorsed his opponent, his opponent went through the roof and he won the primary election in Texas," Trump said.

"And the man that lost, the man that I didn't endorse has become very angry. And that's okay. I understand that. I probably would do the same thing," the president added.

Cornyn, for his part, downplayed that possibility.

"That’s a convenient excuse, and it happens to be untrue," Cornyn told reporters on Capitol Hill Wednesday, according to CBS News.

Trump also told reporters during the Cabinet meeting that though he considers the anti-weaponization fund "dead," he wishes it wasn't.

"Well, it is dead. But you know, I wish it weren't to be honest with you, I think people were horribly treated, horribly abused. This has nothing to do with this was me, horribly abused. And I'd like to see them compensated for the the pain," Trump said.

Blanche is scheduled to appear before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday for a vote on whether to advance his nomination out of the committee and to the full Senate for confirmation.

Fox News Digital contacted the White House, the Justice Department, Cornyn and Tillis for further comment.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

item.title: Jillian Michaels exposes dangers of self-dosing illegal 'gray market' weight loss drugs
item.description: Fitness expert Jillian Michaels warns Americans against self-dosing "gray market" weight-loss peptides, citing health risks like vision loss and hormonal damage.
item.content:encoded:
Fitness expert Jillian Michaels warned Americans against a dangerous trend of buying unregulated, "gray-market" weight-loss peptides online and self-dosing.

Speaking on the "Fox News Rundown," Michaels said foreign-sourced, unapproved chemical compounds pose severe health risks, including potential heart issues, vision loss and hormonal imbalances.

"These are very significant things that need to be further researched and discussed with your doctor before you decide, 'Hey, this sounds like a miracle drug! And I'm buying it on the web, and I am dosing myself in the bathroom off of a Reddit forum,'" Michaels told Fox News' Alex Hogan.

FDA TO REVIEW 7 POPULAR PEPTIDES TOUTED FOR WEIGHT LOSS, HEALING AND LONGEVITY

She noted that although it's "not difficult to get" peptide drugs online, consumers often don't know the true source of the products they’re buying. Michaels warned Americans not to take these drugs "into their own hands," but instead to use them under the supervision of a medical professional.

The federal government has cracked down on illegal sales and dangerous marketing tactics surrounding GLP-1 compounds. In March, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced it had issued 30 warning letters to telehealth companies for making false or misleading claims about compounded GLP-1 products.

MILLIONS COULD GAIN EASIER ACCESS TO POPULAR PEPTIDES AFTER FDA PANEL VOTE

"Compounded drugs can be important for overcoming shortages or meeting unique patient needs — but compounders should not try to compound drugs in a way that circumvents FDA's approval process," FDA Commissioner Marty Makary said in a statement.

In June, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a warning about unapproved GLP-1 drugs, noting that it had logged hundreds of adverse event reports potentially tied to the products. The agency warned that unapproved versions "do not undergo FDA's review for safety, effectiveness and quality before they are marketed" and called out vendors falsely labeling chemicals as "for research purposes only."

Michaels argued that the surge in illegal sales is largely driven by people trying to lose "vanity pounds" quickly after taking inspiration from extreme body transformations in pop culture.

"You've got women in particular, but men as well, in all the major cities that want to go from a size eight to a size two for their summer vacation, and they are getting these things on the gray market. And we're starting to see the results of that in famous celebrities," Michaels said, adding that many people are taking these drugs when they don't need to.

WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS LINKED TO 'OZEMPIC EARS' AND OTHER COSMETIC COMPLAINTS, SURGEONS SAY

"Every week, there's another famous celebrity whose face is being splashed through the headlines and on the front page of different publications… and they look gaunt, they look aged, they're losing their hair. I mean, there are real serious ramifications for this," she added.

While Michaels noted that FDA-approved GLP-1s can be appropriate under medical supervision for individuals with severe obesity or chronic health conditions, she warned that using them or unapproved peptides for minor weight loss carries risks that users overlook.

She pointed to potentially severe side effects, including vision loss and suicidal ideation.

If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

She added that when users stop taking unregulated weight-loss compounds, they often experience an aggressive rebound in hunger.

"You might think, 'Oh, I'm doing this for my summer vacation.' But then when you get off of them, all of a sudden you're hungrier because you've impacted your body's ability to make these hormones naturally," she said.

"And you'll get a cycle of yo-yo dieting that you no longer know how to stop because you messed up your own biochemistry. These things are not a joke, man. They are not something that you play around with for vanity purposes, for sure," Michaels added.

item.title: Bob Barker allegations in explosive docuseries were 'true and then some,' former game show host says
item.description: Former "Double Dare" host Marc Summers recalls Bob Barker's massive ego and cheap pay after Holly Hallstrom detailed her firing from "The Price Is Right" show.
item.content:encoded:
Bob Barker may have been America's beloved game show host, but Marc Summers says there was another side to him behind the scenes.

The former host of Nickelodeon's hit game show "Double Dare" recently appeared on "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia" to celebrate the show's 40th anniversary.

During the interview, Summers was asked about the recent E! docuseries "Dirty Rotten Scandals," which examines allegations that "The Price Is Right" was plagued by a hostile work environment, sexual harassment and discrimination.

OPRAH WINFREY ADMITS SHE BEGGED TALK SHOW AUDIENCE TO BURY FOOTAGE OF WHITNEY HOUSTON ONSTAGE FALL

Summers previously worked with Barker, who died in 2023 at 99.

"Well, I think it’s too bad that the man’s not around to defend himself," the 74-year-old told Sibilia. "However, everything on there was true and then some. I could tell you stories off the air that make your hair curl that were true."

Summers said Barker's ego didn't disappear when the cameras stopped rolling.

WATCH: MARC SUMMERS SAYS BOB BARKER'S EGO ‘WOULDN'T FIT IN THE ROOM’

"When Dorothy Jo (Barker's wife) passed away, he kind of became a different guy, and his ego wouldn't fit in the room," Summers said. "It was all about Bob. On his dressing room door and on his dress shirts, it said, 'WGMC' — 'World's Greatest MC.' Give me a break."

Summers recalled that Studio 33, where "The Price Is Right" was taped, was occasionally used by other productions. During one such shoot, longtime "The Newlywed Game" host Bob Eubanks was filming a pilot when he hid the "WGMC" sign from Barker's dressing room door as a prank.

"So Barker comes in that Monday to do 'Price' and refuses to go on until they find the board that says 'WGMC,' and nobody could find it," Summers said. "They called up Eubanks at home and said, 'What the h--- did you do with this thing? We can't find it.' And Bob cracked up. He said, 'It's under the couch. Just lift up the couch. It is right under there.'"

Looking back, Summers described himself as a 22-year-old "idea man" who got along with Barker. But the price wasn't always right when it came to working for him.

"He had a deal at CBS when they wanted to give him a raise on 'Price,' but they didn't have enough money to pay him more as a host," Summers said.

"So they made him an executive producer and gave him an overall deal. He was producing game shows — or trying to — and needed questions written. He called me at home and said, 'Here's the show. I need 25 questions.' I said, 'Great, how much are you going to pay me?' He said, 'Marc, it's Bob. Don't worry. I'll take care of you.'"

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"So I wanted to impress him," Summers continued. "Instead of giving him 25 questions, I gave him 50. I thought, 'Oh my God, this is going to be great.' I called him and said, 'Bob, let me come by the house and drop them off.' He said, 'No, no, just put them in the mailbox, and there'll be an envelope in there for you.' I wrote him 50 questions when he'd only asked for 25, hoping for a check for $400 or $500. There was a check made out to Marc Summers for the grand total of 50 bucks. So that's the way it was."

WATCH: FAMOUS GAME SHOW HOST BOB BARKER PASSES AWAY AT 99 

In March, Holly Hallstrom claimed on "Dirty Rotten Scandals" that she lost her job on "The Price Is Right" after refusing to publicly stand by Barker when fellow model Dian Parkinson accused him of sexual harassment in a 1994 lawsuit. Hallstrom, one of the show's longtime "Barker's Beauties," said producers blamed her 1995 firing on weight gain caused by medication.

Barker consistently denied wrongdoing and maintained that any relationships were consensual. Fox News Digital reached out to Parkinson for comment.

"When Dian filed her suit, oh boy, that was the beginning of when everything got really bad," Hallstrom told Fox News Digital. "I thought the whole situation, all the publicity, all the media attention, I thought it was horrible. I thought it was tacky. I was glad [co-creator] Mark Goodson had died [in 1992]. He would’ve been mortified to see that kind of tacky scandal on what was a family show."

"I didn't want to be involved in it at all," Hallstrom said. "Barker wanted us to go on all these talk shows and say he was the victim and that Dian was lying. I didn't participate because I thought it was tacky. I also couldn't honestly say, 'Oh yes, Dian is lying,' or 'Oh no, Dian is not lying.' I was not present for those conversations."

"I just avoided doing all of Bob’s PR tour," Hallstrom continued. "Finally, I was told I would be appearing on ‘The Suzanne Somers Show,’ period. And I did. Of course, all they wanted was for me to say that Dian was lying. When Suzanne asked me if I thought Dian was lying, I just babbled some answer, and that was that.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"But then that week, I read in the tabloids, ‘Holly says, ‘Dian is lying.’ I never said that. I called the tabloid and demanded a retraction. They printed a retraction. But that was the beginning of the big rift between Bob and me. That’s when I got on his s--t list."

Parkinson dropped her lawsuit in 1995. At the time, her attorney said the legal battle had become too emotionally and financially draining and had begun affecting her physical health.

"Barker went all over television saying, ‘Her case was dismissed, and I’m totally vindicated,’" Hallstrom recalled. "I said, ‘That’s not true.’ I would not comment on that. I did not participate in those interviews. ... I would not change my testimony to suit Barker. That’s when I was told my weight was a problem. I was off the show."

"That was, well, probably the worst thing in my life at that point that had ever happened," Hallstrom admitted. "It only got worse from there."

Hallstrom and Barker spent nearly a decade locked in a legal battle after he sued her for defamation, according to Business Insider. She filed a countersuit alleging defamation, emotional distress and discrimination.

According to the outlet, Hallstrom said she was effectively blacklisted in the entertainment industry and pushed to the brink financially. She also declined settlement offers, saying she refused to be silenced by a nondisclosure agreement.

Two days before Hallstrom's case was scheduled to go to trial, Barker and CBS agreed to settle, Business Insider reported. According to the outlet, CBS agreed to pay Hallstrom a settlement reportedly worth millions. The terms were not disclosed, and the settlement did not constitute an admission of wrongdoing.

"I was not going to sign a nondisclosure for that show or anything," she said. "I was not going to sign away my right to free speech. It also meant that Barker could not do to me what he did to Dian, go out and claim victory and vindication. ... He could not say anything about me as long as I could speak out for myself. And he never said another word."

Not everyone accepted the show's portrayal of Barker. His longtime publicist defended the late host as "beloved" and "the greatest MC in TV history," while longtime producer Roger Dobkowitz denounced the series as an "obvious hit piece," arguing "The Price Is Right" "was a happy place" for most employees.

item.title: Hunter Biden claims under oath that his family is broke amid fight over $17M legal bill
item.description: Hunter Biden claims in a deposition that he has no assets, no car, and no savings as a law firm sues him for $17 million in unpaid legal bills.
item.content:encoded:
In a recently released deposition transcript, Hunter Biden claimed that his family is broke and that he’s being crushed by legal fees.

The deposition is related to an ongoing lawsuit between Biden and firm Winston Taylor for unpaid legal bills. Winston Taylor, which has a history of representing leading Democrats, claims that the Biden scion owes them $17 million from representing him in criminal prosecutions, congressional investigations and defamation suits against his critics.

"My family doesn't have any money, and it's not their debt anyway," he said, according to the transcript. "I don't own anything of any value other than — and I don't know the value of it — my paintings which I painted myself. So that's it. And I don't even have any other assets at all, stocks, bonds, anything like that, savings accounts."

HUNTER BIDEN RESURFACES IN LA, REACTS TO QUESTIONS ABOUT BIDEN TAPES, UFO FILES

Claims that the Biden family may be strapped for cash are reflected in other reporting.

The Wall Street Journal reported in September 2025 that former President Joe Biden is having far more trouble cashing in on his time in the White House than his predecessors.

Upon leaving office, the former president had accrued roughly $800,000 in personal debt and was burdened with increased property taxes on their $2.7 million Delaware home, according to a source familiar with his finances. Biden also has had trouble booking paid speaking engagements, a common source of funds for former presidents, owing to his unpopularity and fears of angering President Donald Trump.

CHARLAMAGNE RIPS JILL BIDEN’S CONFESSIONS ABOUT HER HUSBAND AS TOO LITTLE, TOO LATE

Former President Joe Biden, however, pulls in more than $400,000 a year in government pensions from his time in Congress and the White House, according to the National Taxpayers Union Foundation.

Hunter Biden’s claimed lack of assets follows years of partying and substance abuse.

The former president’s son reportedly spent large sums of cash on crack cocaine, alcohol, stays at luxury hotels, prostitutes and expensive jewelry for his brother’s widow, whom he was romantically involved with. His spending habits could help explain how he blew through the wealth he accumulated selling paintings and pulling in a seven-figure salary while employed by the Ukrainian energy company Burisma.

‘PRIVILEGED’ HUNTER BIDEN, SPARED BY DAD’S PARDON, BLASTS TRUMP’S CLEMENCY POWER

"I don't have any assets. I don't own a car. I don't own a phone," Biden said in the deposition, which took place in February but was released by Biden’s new lawyers in recent days.

Biden argues that Winston Taylor knew he would be unable to pay his legal fees when it agreed to take him on as a client and claims the parties agreed to "work something out." The law firm, meanwhile, says that it tried to connect Biden with donors in the Democratic ecosystem to help him cover his legal bills.

The younger Biden won a comparatively small legal victory in July when a judge awarded him $1.7 million in a defamation suit. Winston Taylor, however, has sought to put a lien on the judgment, and the Overstock CEO Patrick Byrne, who was ruled against, is believed to be overseas, making collection complicated.

Representatives for Hunter Biden and former President Joe Biden did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital Friday.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Reflecting pool controversy is mirror for our broken politics
item.description: Jeanine Pirro dropped charges against David Hearn after documents revealed the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool damage stemmed from flawed contractor work.
item.content:encoded:
In the 104 years that the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has stood on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., the event it is most closely associated with is the 1963 "I Have a Dream," speech by the Rev. Martin Luther King, Jr., but today, far from a symbol of national unity, this body of water has created a wave of anger and discontent.

On Friday, United States Attorney for the District of Washington, D.C. Jeanine Pirro did the right thing and dropped charges against David Hearn, a former Olympic athlete who had been facing 10 years in jail for allegedly defacing the monument.

Hearn was accused of pulling up pieces of the new sealant installed this year during President Donald Trump’s renovation of the pool. He claims he was just curious about the pre-existing damage he saw.

FORMER US OLYMPIAN DAVID HEARN INDICTED IN ALLEGED REFLECTING POOL VANDALISM

It may have been as annoying as chipping away at dried paint, but it wasn’t a felony.

According to the motion filed Friday, additional documents showed that the damage to the reflecting pool was the result of flawed installation by the contractor.

The first thing to say here is good for Pirro, who, unlike former President Biden’s Department of Justice in many January 6 and abortion protest cases, did not allow primal politics to influence her legal decision. That is how this is supposed to work.

WHITE HOUSE CONDEMNS 'TARGETED SABOTAGE' OF REFLECTING POOL AS REPAIRS PUSHED PAST JULY 4 CELEBRATION

What matters here is that the reason that Hearn’s curiosity, politically driven or otherwise, caused this kerfuffle, is that Trump’s repair of the reflecting pool, a public works project that should be as mundane as installing a stop sign, has become a synecdoche for America’s political divide.

To Trump’s critics, such as independent journalist Jim Acosta, who has all but camped out by the pool for months, this is a prime example of cronyism, Trump lining his friends’ pockets as they fail to properly line this national treasure.

It was with glee that leftists celebrated the peeling of sealant and the growth of algae in the pool, as if nature itself was confirming all of their anti-Trump convictions.

TOP TRUMP OFFICIAL TOUTS HOW DC MAKEOVER IS PROOF AMERICA IS REJECTING 'DECLINE BY CHOICE'

But one big flaw in this argument is exposed by a 2012 Washington Post headline, after work had been done on the pool, that blared, "Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool Is Drained To Remove Algae." So, unless then-President Obama was also a corrupt cronyist, it might just be that the reflecting pool is not easy to maintain.

The fault in this situation, as Pirro rightly points out, is with the Department of the Interior, for telling President Trump what he wanted to hear instead of the truth. To the extent that it put Hearn’s freedom at risk, that was utterly unacceptable.

But at the same time, in this day and age, was it so crazy for Interior to think that a deranged leftist was intentionally trying to damage the monument? Such things are par for the course for the looney left, and why was Hearns pulling at the sealant, anyway?

By all accounts, the beautification, not to mention the increased safety, of the capital since Trump activated the National Guard last year has been little short of miraculous. You can tell because unlike ICE agents, Democrats aren’t calling the Guard fascists.

Fountains are flowing, businesses are growing, Capitol Hill staffers in their drab dress and loafers roam the streets without fear. But by all means, let’s obsess over a minor setback to repair on a pool unlike any in the world.

The reflecting pool is now a microcosm of everything broken in our politics, our focus on meaningless minutiae and blindness to anything that does not confirm our worst suspicions.

The conventional wisdom in Washington circles will suggest that Trump must be furious at Pirro for undermining his narrative that vandals are to blame for the renovation’s imperfections. But I doubt it. In fact, this is the exit ramp from the story that he needed.

In the summer of 1963, King brought the country together around the reflecting pool and helped our nation to dream of unity and peace. In 2026, this shimmering oasis in the swamp represents little but Americans' contempt for one another.

In this case, thanks to Pirro, the proper result was arrived at after all the sturm und drang. But in the end, the only way to stop such madness is for all of us, every American, to stop assuming the worst about those with whom we disagree.

item.title: Bill Maher warns that the Democratic Party is being 'colonized' by socialists, says his 'vote is in play'
item.description: Bill Maher says his vote is in play, blasting the Democratic party for being "colonized" by socialist views and the DSA's growing influence.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian and talk show host Bill Maher doubled down on his previous comments suggesting his "vote is in play" in coming elections, as he expressed his discontent over the Democratic Party being "colonized" by radical, socialist views.

During Friday night’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," Maher blasted the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) agenda that appears to be taking hold within the mainstream Democratic Party.

"People gotta realize this is going on," Maher said. "Yes, my vote is in play. I'm not voting for anyone who thinks the wrong side won the Cold War or cheers for the intifada like it's the World Cup."

MAHER SHAMES CLINTONS, KAMALA, DEMS, SAYING THEY WON'T GO ON HIS SHOW OR ANYWHERE THEY AREN'T 'PRE-ADORED'

Maher went on to poke fun at the sheer irony of the apparent political takeover within a party that has platformed against such views.

"It's so ironic from the people who obsess about colonization," Maher said. "You know what's being colonized now? The Democratic Party."

He then pointed to two congressional Democrats — Rep. Tom Suozzi, D-N.Y., and Rep. Adam Gray, D-Calif.— after the pair launched a pledge to moderate the party amid the internal rise in DSA views.

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

"Last month, two Democratic congressmen released an open pledge," Maher told the audience. "They wanted their fellow Democratic members to sign. It said, ‘We are capitalists, not socialists. We want safety, not lawlessness. We are proud, not ashamed of America.’ These should not be hard words for a congressional Democrat to sign onto."

"You know how many did?" Maher continued. "Eight [members]. Eight, out of 212."

He added that while the DSA platform may appear to be making waves throughout the party, most mainstream politicians do not align themselves with the radical-left views.

SEN MARK KELLY WARNS FAR-LEFT POLICIES THAT ‘DON’T MAKE SENSE’ COULD COST DEMOCRATS SEATS

"And, no, this nonsense is not where most Democratic politicians are right now," Maher said. "But it's also becoming a raging fire festival in the party that neither is anyone putting out."

"People are actually getting elected now who literally don't think we should have police or prisons or borders," he added.

Maher’s comments come after Fox News Digital previously reported he told ABC News "This Week" co-anchor Jonathan Karl that his "vote is in play" due to his unhappiness with the direction the Democratic party is heading.

"My vote is in play because it can’t be Trump running, so I’m not living in communist America," Maher said last month.

"I mean, I know the talking point is that it’s not communism, it’s socialism. OK, I’ve read the quotes from the DSA platform from their own mouths. Don’t tell me I’m not seeing what I am seeing," he added at the time.

The sentiment was echoed by former state attorney Dave Aronberg, who told Fox News Digital the DSA's platform could be what brings an end to the Democrats' short-lived momentum in the polls.

"History and current polling trends point to a blue wave in November, and the DSA is the only thing that can stop it," Aronberg said. "Outside of concentrated blue enclaves in places like New York and Denver, general elections aren't won on the far-left fringes.
